newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Most Swissair units improve H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Most Swissair units improve H1 results.

text.p: Swissair AG said most of its units improved their performance in the first half of the year, but the impact on the result had largely been offset by currency fluctuations and lower profits on the sale of fixed assets.
Higher fuel costs and a sluggish Swiss economy also adversely affected Swissair results.
Swissair reported a net loss of 51 million Swiss francs for January-June 1996, down from the 86 million loss last year.

Despite an 8.0 percent increase in traffic volume, flight operations also had to contend with a further five percent drop in yield. Unit costs fell 7.0 percent so the deficit was smaller than in 1995.
The cargo/logistics division was plagued by sluggish international trade, overcapacity and declining margins.
But technical services and ground services exceeded their budgeted objectives, despite increased competition.
Crossair, Swissair's regional airline subsidiary, reported satisfactory results despite taking over Swissair's short-haul operations and having to compete in a fiercely-contested market place.
The results of Swissair Associated Cos (SAC), Swissair's holding for non-flight operations, clearly improved from last year and were in line with the budget, Swissair said.
